newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Belgolaise takes over Barclays Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: Belgolaise takes over Barclays Ivory Coast.

text.p: Banque Atlantique Cote d'Ivoire (BACI), part of Belgian bank Belgolaise SA, has taken over the Ivory Coast operation of Barclays Plc, with effect from June 14.
An official at BACI said BACI had taken on all the staff employed by Barclays and planned in particular to develop its under-used foreign exchange department and its business services.
A Barclays spokeswoman in London said Barclays had been looking to sell the Ivory Coast business for a long time as it was not one of its core countries of operation in Africa.
She said it would continue to concentrate on Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Kenya.

Belgolaise, which is part of Societe Generale de Belgique SA has been expanding rapidly in Africa, buying stakes in banks in Niger, Togo, Ghana and Uganda in 1996 to give it a presence in 17 sub-Saharan countries.
Part of this expansion has involved buying stakes in six banks that were part of the Meridien group of African banks that collapsed in early 1995.
